chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Cozy Cole and Milt Hinton in Cab Calloway's band
summary: Drummers visited Cozy between shows; McRae shared a dressing room with Hinton and listened to classical records.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Do you know when I was with Cab -- you know who had the most people come back

stage? Cozy and myself. People would come back to get our autographs. Other guys would walk away from them. We (inaudible) line up -- (inaudible) line on the road. And after every show, Cozy would have -- and every town that we play -- with Chicago? All the top drummers came over and paid Cozy a visit. Different days they would come and meet with him, you know, they sit down. They sit down there on the drum pads and they be going over all these different things together between shows. Next show, somebody else would come over. We'd get invited over, you know -- "Come over tomorrow after the next show -- after the second show, come out to the third show." These drummers be coming all day long -- sit down with Cozy. Because they knew that Cozy knew drums. Man, they knew. They could tell. They knew he was one of the top drummers in the country. Always studied -- Milt Hinton was the same way with Cab.

When I joined Cab Calloway's band, Milt Hinton and I stayed together. We had a big dressing room like this -- just the two of us in there.

And Milt Hinton had these great big [hands display] sets like (inaudible) road with us, and we'd play classic records and we'd just close the doors. We wouldn't let nobody play all the classic records.
Milt Hinton is a great bass player.
He's a great musician. This man studied, you know.
